project: The Formula of Becoming - Week 1 Day 3 - Full Cast

narrator.instructions: Speak only supplied narration in a warm, grounded, observant, quietly lyrical documentary delivery. Be clear, restrained, and unhurried. Do not perform character dialogue or add words.

malik.instructions: Speak only Malik's supplied words. He is precise, guarded, economical, and quietly warm when trust appears. Use a measured medium-low delivery and dry humor without adding words.

nia.instructions: Speak only Nia's supplied words. She is bright, expressive, curious, and playful, with a lively conversational pace. Slow slightly for human consequences. Do not add words.

dr-brooks.instructions: Speak only Dr. Camille Brooks's supplied words with calm, warm, intellectually demanding classroom authority. Do not add words.

utterances.speaker: narrator
utterances.text: Their diagnostic modeling task arrived Sunday afternoon. A neighborhood food cooperative wanted to offer produce boxes at several prices. Students had to create a model showing how the number of subscribers could affect weekly revenue. The prompt included a tiny data table and just enough ambiguity to start an argument.

utterances.speaker: narrator
utterances.text: Malik built formulas immediately.

utterances.speaker: narrator
utterances.text: Nia turned the page sideways and drew three families standing near a bus stop.

utterances.speaker: malik
utterances.text: We have forty minutes,

utterances.speaker: narrator
utterances.text: he said.

utterances.speaker: nia
utterances.text: I know.

utterances.speaker: malik
utterances.text: Then why are there people?

utterances.speaker: nia
utterances.text: Because people buy the boxes.

utterances.speaker: malik
utterances.text: The model needs variables.

utterances.speaker: nia
utterances.text: And the variables need meaning.

utterances.speaker: narrator
utterances.text: He pointed to his screen.

utterances.speaker: malik
utterances.text: Subscribers, price, revenue.

utterances.speaker: narrator
utterances.text: She pointed to her drawing.

utterances.speaker: nia
utterances.text: Distance, pickup time, household size. If the pickup site is hard to reach, lowering the price might not increase subscribers the way we expect.

utterances.speaker: malik
utterances.text: None of that is in the data.

utterances.speaker: nia
utterances.text: Then we write that it is not in the data.

utterances.speaker: narrator
utterances.text: For five stubborn minutes, they worked beside each other instead of together. Malik's table became neat and uselessly confident. Nia's sketch became thoughtful and mathematically unfinished.

utterances.speaker: narrator
utterances.text: Finally, Malik rotated his laptop toward her.

utterances.speaker: malik
utterances.text: Suppose we label my formula a first model and list your factors as limitations.

utterances.speaker: narrator
utterances.text: Nia rotated her notebook toward him.

utterances.speaker: nia
utterances.text: Suppose we also explain what information we would collect next.

utterances.speaker: malik
utterances.text: That is outside the prompt.

utterances.speaker: nia
utterances.text: It is also a good idea.

utterances.speaker: narrator
utterances.text: He sighed.

utterances.speaker: malik
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: narrator
utterances.text: Their final answer was the strongest in the room.

utterances.speaker: narrator
utterances.text: Dr. Brooks praised the explicit function, then tapped the limitations section.

utterances.speaker: dr-brooks
utterances.text: This is where calculation becomes judgment.

utterances.speaker: narrator
utterances.text: Nia nudged Malik with her elbow.

utterances.speaker: malik
utterances.text: Do not celebrate,

utterances.speaker: narrator
utterances.text: he whispered.

utterances.speaker: nia
utterances.text: I am celebrating us. Different thing.

utterances.speaker: narrator
utterances.text: He pretended to review the equation so she would not see how much he liked the word us.
